nodes.label: Batched Breaking Release
nodes.rationale: Pending breaking changes are collected so they can be released together rather than causing repeated compatibility breaks.

nodes.label: Icon Design Guidelines
nodes.rationale: Consistent dimensions, strokes, naming, and simplified SVG structure make icons visually coherent across hundreds of unlabeled actions.

nodes.label: Hostile-Code Security Model
nodes.rationale: The sandbox assumes untrusted code is maximally hostile, while documenting that language servers and writable project metadata can still escape the default profile.

nodes.label: File-Descriptor Bind Validation
nodes.rationale: Open O_PATH descriptors pin writable inodes so the in-sandbox bridge can reject a bind whose path was swapped between validation and mounting.

nodes.label: Seccomp IPC-Socket Protection
nodes.rationale: Read-only mounts do not prevent connecting to Unix sockets, so a seccomp filter blocks creation of socket families that could escape the sandbox while preserving loopback proxy traffic.

nodes.label: HostFilesystemLocation
nodes.rationale: Sensitive APIs capture and validate a host path once, reducing races caused by repeated canonicalization.

nodes.label: TerminalBuilder Two-Step Instantiation
nodes.rationale: TTY creation can fail, but GPUI models cannot fail to instantiate, so TerminalBuilder separates fallible handle creation from context-bound subscription.

nodes.label: Backend-Neutral Terminal Boundary
nodes.rationale: Keeping Alacritty conversions near the event loop allows future backend experiments without UI-wide refactors.

nodes.label: Neovim Result Cache
nodes.rationale: Cached Neovim results keep normal CI runs fast while the feature flag refreshes expected behavior during development.

nodes.label: Distinct Product Identity
nodes.rationale: The palette deliberately differs from Zed blue so ZOrca cannot be mistaken for Zed in an application dock.

nodes.label: Build Optimization Order
nodes.rationale: Fix broad cache invalidation and unnecessary debuginfo first, then reduce development LTO, cache licenses, and only afterward benchmark parallelism, linkers, larger runners, and sccache.

nodes.label: --force-warn Requirement
nodes.rationale: After -A warnings disables the warning group, --force-warn reliably re-enables a driver-registered Dylint whereas a plain -W may not.

nodes.label: Cargo Fingerprint Clean
nodes.rationale: DYLINT_RUSTFLAGS is absent from Cargo fingerprints, so targeted packages must be cleaned to avoid replaying stale lint results.

nodes.label: Commit Message Structure
nodes.rationale: A fixed type, optional scope, imperative description, body, and footer produce standardized and descriptive commit messages.

nodes.label: Vocabulary Discipline
nodes.rationale: One word, one meaning, and one part of speech reduce ambiguity and synonym rotation in technical text.

nodes.label: Technical Communication Adaptations
nodes.rationale: Short sentences, one meaning per word, and condition-first commands transfer to technical text where misreading has a cost.

nodes.label: Plain-Language Replacement
nodes.rationale: Overused words are replaced with plain equivalents, while words that carry no fact are deleted.

nodes.label: Selective Hard-Fork Contribution Model
nodes.rationale: ZOrca carries a wide diff from Zed, so large changes require prior discussion and applicable upstream fixes are ported selectively.

nodes.label: Worktree-Isolated Agent Workspace
nodes.rationale: Each agent receives a separate Git worktree so concurrent agents do not modify the same checkout.

nodes.label: Agent Execution Trust Boundary
nodes.rationale: Agent presets intentionally disable their own permission prompts, and a Git worktree is not a sandbox, so destructive agent behavior under those flags is out of scope.

nodes.label: Request-Scoped Failure Boundary
nodes.rationale: The envelope moves unknown-operation and malformed-body failures from the connection to the one request so a bad request cannot take down live attachments.

nodes.label: Stable Error Frames
nodes.rationale: Stable machine-readable codes distinguish operational failures without parsing human prose.

nodes.label: Generation Handshake
nodes.rationale: The daemon selects one generation and the client verifies it, giving one authority for compatibility mismatch diagnosis.

nodes.label: Additive Protocol Evolution
nodes.rationale: Unknown fields are ignored and new operations are capability-gated so protocol changes remain survivable after the one-time cut.

nodes.label: Forced Replacement Requires Consent
nodes.rationale: Replacing a pre-cut busy daemon can terminate live PTYs, so the desktop must explain the cost and proceed only after explicit human confirmation.

nodes.label: Fixed Wire Constraints
nodes.rationale: A stable versionless socket lets Rust and Python daemons compete for one endpoint, while fixed length-prefixed JSON avoids split encodings.

nodes.label: Persist-Before-Ack Contract
nodes.rationale: A successful mutation acknowledgement must imply durable recording; persistence failure must be visible to the requester.

nodes.label: FIFO Persist Worker
nodes.rationale: One FIFO worker with enqueue-time snapshots prevents stale snapshots from overwriting newer state by construction.

nodes.label: Degraded Persistence Mode
nodes.rationale: Success with persisted false keeps sessions usable against a newer read-only ledger without claiming durability or inviting duplicate retries.

nodes.label: Stale Folder-Key Cleanup
nodes.rationale: A persisted folder-path key became visible after a rename moved the workspace; the shared WorktreePathsChanged handler removes it when no retained workspace owns it.

nodes.label: Stable Repository-Key Fix
nodes.rationale: During a worktree move the repository model disappears temporarily, so the sidebar uses the snapshot's stable root repository directory instead of classifying the open root as standalone.

nodes.label: Managed Center-Terminal Fix
nodes.rationale: Generic center-terminal helpers created unmanaged shells that layout capture omitted, so the ADE layout owner intercepts the helper and creates a managed persistent session.

nodes.label: Pre-Cut Daemon Recovery Proposal
nodes.rationale: This investigation proposed a bounded legacy attach path because a plain-terminal fallback competes with the original live Codex writer; a later investigation corrected that proposal.

nodes.label: Bounded Generation-One Reconnect
nodes.rationale: This historical answer added one bounded generation-one reconnect after handshake retry while preserving daemon-owned PTYs.

nodes.label: Generation-Two-Only Forced Upgrade
nodes.rationale: The correction rejects generation-one reconnects: report incompatibility, require destructive-upgrade confirmation, then force-stop and replace the old daemon without opening a competing terminal.

nodes.label: Layout Revision Race Fix
nodes.rationale: An event could echo a new layout revision before the control ack and rebuild the pane; claiming the revision before send preserves pane identity and rolling it back handles refusal.
